overview.description: Pinochle is a classic card game that combines two distinct phases: **melding** (showing combinations of cards for points) and **trick-taking** (winning individual tricks to score additional points). Played with a unique 48-card deck containing two copies of each card from 9 to Ace, Pinochle offers deep strategic gameplay centered around the auction/bidding phase where players compete to name the trump suit.

history.origins: Pinochle traces its roots to the German card game Binokel (also spelled Binocle), which emerged in the mid-19th century. The name "Pinochle" is believed to derive from the French word "binocle" meaning "eyeglasses" or "pince-nez," possibly referring to the paired nature of the double deck.
timeline: Mid-19th century: Binokel emerges in Germany (from bezique).
Late 19th century: German immigrants bring Binokel to USA; name becomes Pinochle.

nullReasons.evolution: No documented evolutionary changes; game emerged as a stable tradition.

setup.players: 4 players in fixed partnerships (partners sit opposite).
setup.deck: 48-card Pinochle deck (two copies each of 9, 10, J, Q, K, A in all four suits).
setup.dealing:
1. Shuffle the 48-card deck thoroughly
2. Deal 12 cards to each player (in batches of 3 or 4 cards)
3. Rotation: Deal rotates clockwise after each hand

rules.objective: Score points through melding and trick-taking. The declarer's team must make at least the bid amount or the bid is deducted from their score. First team to the target score wins.
rules.gameplay: 1. Bid (min 250). Declarer names trump; partner passes 4 cards to declarer, declarer passes 4 back. 2. All four players lay meld face-up. 3. Declarer leads first trick. Must follow suit; highest wins. Counters (A, 10, K) score 10 pts each; last trick 10. If declarer's team fails the bid, bid is deducted.
keyRules: Rank: A, 10, K, Q, J, 9 (Ten second highest).
Counters in tricks = 10 pts each; last trick = 10.
Racehorse: partner passes 4 to declarer before play.

strategy.basic: Bid on strength: runs, marriages, aces. Pass best trump to declarer. Lead trump to draw opponents' trumps. Save high counters for tricks. Melds matter especially near the end.
strategy.intermediate: Meld order: show runs and marriages first. Save high counters for tricks. Don't overbid with weak hands.
strategy.advanced: Count meld and trick points. Declarer needs ~250 from meld plus tricks. Passing: send aces and trump; get back non-counters.

difficulty.medium: Bids on meld strength; passes trump to declarer; leads trump to draw.
difficulty.hard: Full meld and trick counting; optimal passing; partnership coordination.

considerations: Meld evaluation for bidding. Trick play with double cards. Passing phase (4 cards) is critical.

phases.label: Bidding
phases.notes: Auction until three pass; high bidder declares trump.

phases.label: Pass cards
phases.notes: Partner passes 4 to declarer; declarer passes 4 back (racehorse).

phases.label: Melding
phases.notes: All four show melds; bid winner first; points counted.

phases.label: Play
phases.notes: Declarer leads; 12 tricks; follow suit; counters score 10 each; last trick 10.

play_card.description: Play one card to the trick. Follow suit if possible; if void, may play trump. Highest card of led suit wins, or highest trump if trump led.
play_card.constraints: Must follow suit when able; when void may trump. Declarer leads first trick; trick winner leads next. Identical cards: first played wins.

pass.description: Partner passes cards to declarer; declarer passes same number back. Typically 4 cards in partnership pinochle.
pass.constraints: Only after trump is declared; partner passes first, then declarer.

bid.description: Bid points predicted from meld and tricks; highest bidder declares trump. Minimum opening bid often 250 (or 100).
bid.constraints: Bids in multiples of 10; must be higher than previous; pass drops out. Player to dealer's left may be forced to open.

meld.description: Display combinations face-up for points: runs, marriages, arounds, pinochle, dix. One card per meld type per heading.
meld.constraints: All four players meld after passing; bid winner melds first. Cards stay on table until counted.

go_out.reason: This game has no go-out action.

trumpConfig.trumpSuitRanking: Jack of trump (Jick) and Queen of trump (Spad) are highest; then A, 10, K, 9.
trumpConfig.overtakingRule: Must follow suit; when void may play trump; must overtrump if possible when trump is led (post-1945: only when trump led).

edgeCases.text: When two identical cards are played to a trick, the first played wins.
Renege: misplay (e.g. not following suit, sloughing when holding trump) causes penalty; bidder renege = double set; defender renege = bidder makes bid.
Misdeal: some versions allow redeal if a player is dealt five nines (and no aces).

engine.deckDescription: A 48-card Pinochle deck: four French suits, each with two copies of 9, 10, Jack, Queen, King, Ace (no 2–8). Used for melding and trick-taking; players bid, meld, and play tricks; scoring combines meld points and trick points.
engine.suitDescription: The four French suits (hearts, diamonds, clubs, spades) each have twelve cards (two each of 9 through Ace). In Pinochle, trump is determined by bid; marriage and other melds use both suit and rank; following suit applies in tricks.
engine.rankDescription: In Pinochle order, 9 is low then 10, Jack, Queen, King, Ace high; the Jack of trump (Jick) and Queen of trump (Spad) are the two highest trumps. Rank determines trick winners and meld values (e.g. marriage, run, pinochle).
engine.dealPattern: Clockwise, 3 or 4 cards at a time to each player; all 48 dealt (12 each).

scoring.description: Meld points plus trick points. Counters (A, 10, K) = 10 pts each; last trick = 10.
scoring.winCondition: First team to target score (often 1000). Bid and make to add; fail bid = subtract bid.

penalties.Fail bid: Bid amount subtracted from team score.
